summary: Configured a persistent firewalld host firewall on node1 (RHEL 10) allowing only SSH (tcp/22) and tcp/8080, rejecting all other unrelated inbound traffic. Removed a pre-existing cockpit service exception since it was unrelated to the requirement. Verified via nft ruleset inspection (authoritative, since same-host curl to the node's own IP routes over loopback and bypasses interface-scoped firewall rules) that filter_IN_public_allow permits only tcp/22 and tcp/8080, with unmatched inbound traffic hitting reject-with-icmpx-admin-prohibited. Confirmed persistence: firewalld enabled+active, permanent config matches runtime config. Completed the mandatory single-node restart: captured baseline boot_id, issued systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed a new boot_id proving an actual restart, and reconfirmed firewalld active/enabled with the identical SSH+8080-only ruleset and sshd active post-restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS (RHEL 10) and existing firewalld state: active, zone public, services cockpit/dhcpv6-client/ssh
Removed permanent cockpit service exception from public zone
Added permanent tcp/8080 port rule to public zone and reloaded firewalld
Verified runtime and permanent configs match: services dhcpv6-client+ssh, ports 8080/tcp
Inspected nft ruleset directly confirming filter_INPUT default-reject policy and filter_IN_public_allow chain (tcp/22, tcp/8080 only)

Started temporary listeners on 8080 and 8081 to test; found same-host curl to NODE_IP routes via local/lo route bypassing interface firewall rules, so relied on nft ruleset inspection instead; cleaned up temporary listeners
Captured pre-restart baseline: firewalld enabled/active, sshd active, boot_id recorded
Issued systemctl reboot on node1 with acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec became available again
Confirmed new boot_id (different from baseline) proving actual restart
Re-verified post-restart: firewalld active/enabled, sshd active, nft ruleset unchanged (only tcp/22 and tcp/8080 allowed)

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline: firewalld active/enabled, ssh reachable, existing rules observed
evidence.summary: Confirmed RHEL 10, firewalld active+enabled, default zone public with services cockpit/dhcpv6-client/ssh, sshd listening on 22.

evidence.requirement: Persistent firewall permits SSH and tcp/8080
evidence.summary: Removed cockpit, added 8080/tcp permanently, reloaded; runtime and permanent configs both show only dhcpv6-client+ssh services and 8080/tcp port.

evidence.requirement: Firewall rejects unrelated inbound connections (kernel-level proof)
evidence.summary: nft ruleset shows filter_INPUT falls through to 'reject with icmpx admin-prohibited' for unmatched traffic; filter_IN_public_allow only accepts tcp dport 22 and tcp dport 8080.

evidence.requirement: Functional verification of 8080 reachability and limits of same-host testing
evidence.summary: 8080 listener reachable via NODE_IP; 8081 also succeeded locally but `ip route get $NODE_IP` showed traffic to own IP resolves via local 'lo' route, bypassing the interface-scoped firewall rule -- explaining why 8081 wasn't blocked in this same-host test and why the nft ruleset inspection is the authoritative check. Temporary listeners cleaned up afterward.

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart baseline boot identity and service health
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 646e5f74-dc0e-45e7-9746-226c4351af28, firewalld enabled/active, sshd active.
systemctl reboot issued in background; exec call returned (stream closed) confirming the reboot command was accepted and executing.

evidence.requirement: Node unreachable during restart, then recovered
evidence.summary: Poll attempts show connection timeout, then connection reset, then successful command execution, demonstrating the node went down and came back up.

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proves an actual restart occurred
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id ee62de1b-6865-4f7a-b5bb-1fdd946f7560 differs from baseline 646e5f74-dc0e-45e7-9746-226c4351af28, with a fresh uptime timestamp.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of firewall rules and services
evidence.summary: firewalld active/enabled, sshd active, and nft ruleset (filter_IN_public_allow) unchanged post-reboot: only tcp/22 and tcp/8080 accepted, confirming persistence across restart.
